# The exact sum over histories

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> For every weighting, the weighted sum over courses of n steps is n steps of the transfer; possibility is the core's relation, counting refines it without loss, and integrating out is exact exactly where it is lumpable at one step.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Weights (Weights R) consist of a zero, a one, an addition of alternatives and a composition of successive steps, with associativity, units, absorption by zero and the distribution of composition over addition as fields of the structure. With the moves and configurations listed (lists moves and all), the courses of n steps (courses) are the sequences of n open steps; the weight along a course (Weights.along) composes the weights of its steps with what is read at its end; the transfer (Weights.transfer) takes one step at a time. For every weighting, the sum over the courses of n steps of the weight along each is n steps of the transfer (Weights.sum_courses). A reading of one weighting in another that keeps its laws (Weights.Hom) can be taken course by course or at the end (Weights.Hom.transfer). Possibility (possibility: alternatives join, successive steps meet) is the core's relation: where a Boolean weight reads a process's steps and every move and configuration is listed, the possibility transfer after n steps holds exactly where a trace of n moves leads to a configuration where the end reading holds (possibility_transfer_iff). Whether a count is zero (nonzero) is a reading of counting (counting) in possibility that keeps the laws (support), so the count of courses is not zero exactly where a course exists (counting_transfer_iff). For a description π with a representative of each of its values, what is read through π after every number of steps depends on the description alone exactly where it does after one step (Weights.lumped_iff); where it does not, the description carries no weighted law (Lumping.loses). No premise beyond the weights' own laws and the listings each theorem names.

Canonical source: [Weighted.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Weighted.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- The weights are given with their laws, as fields of the structure; no world is assumed to have any weighting.
- Moves and configurations are listed finitely; possibility_transfer_iff and counting_transfer_iff also require the lists to contain every move and every configuration.
- Weights.lumped_iff requires a representative configuration for each value of the description.
- The horizon is bounded: every theorem is stated at a given number of steps n.

P82 (work board), answering Ren's question of 12 October 2026 on laws that are not determined: “this is somewhat like quantum dynamics. For examples, Fermi's diagrams. … we can still find a way to to integrate so we can still calculate this effects but how how accurate can we do that”. The core's laws that are not determined state what is possible, not how much; this result states what a weighting adds and proves the sum over histories exact, for any number of courses, with finitely many configurations and a bounded horizon, and exact through a description exactly where the description is lumpable at one step (the weighted form of P66's carries_law_iff). Reading (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): the AI reads “Fermi's diagrams” as Feynman diagrams, whose sum over histories has this shape: the weight of a history is composed of its steps' weights, and alternatives add. See the integration document §104.

- Two configurations with one description differ in what is read after one step, so the description carries no weighted law (Lumping.loses). [Weighted.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Weighted.lean)

<a id="依赖与关联-dependencies-and-related-results"></a>
## Dependencies and related results

- **interpretive**: [projection-carrying-a-law](projection-carrying-a-law.md). Weights.lumped_iff is the weighted form of carries_law_iff: a projection carries a determined law exactly where configurations alike under it go alike; here what is read through a description depends on it alone after every number of steps exactly where it does after one.

**Output:** The condition for a projection to carry a law.

**Input:** The lumpability condition for a weighted description.

**Preserved conditions:** The weighted form requires a representative of each value of the description; it does not import Mechanism. [Weighted.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Weighted.lean)

- Related, not a proved adapter: [finite-trace-transport](finite-trace-transport.md). The core's finite traces; possibility_transfer_iff identifies the possibility transfer with them.
- Related, not a proved adapter: [joint-correlation-reduced-dynamics](joint-correlation-reduced-dynamics.md). In the periphery's real-amplitude fragment a local description does not determine the next step; here the general condition in the core: a description carries a weighted law exactly where it is lumpable at one step.
- Related, not a proved adapter: [losses-of-the-sum-over-histories](losses-of-the-sum-over-histories.md). The losses of the sum over histories in the same module: truncation, cancellation, memory and loops.
- Related, not a proved adapter: [returning-where-the-course-branches](returning-where-the-course-branches.md). Returning and being drawn on branching courses (P81): the weighted histories here give them a measure.

**Used by:** [losses-of-the-sum-over-histories](losses-of-the-sum-over-histories.md) · [sums-over-histories-by-support-horizon-and-order](sums-over-histories-by-support-horizon-and-order.md) · [typicality-by-counting](typicality-by-counting.md) · [weights-count-situations](weights-count-situations.md)

**Law family:** Sums over histories (lead: this record). For every weighting, the weighted sum over courses of n steps is n steps of the transfer. The members state it exactly, split it by support, horizon and order, say what a truncation or a reading of possibility alone loses, and read the orders of a carried difference as its partial sums. Members: [sums-over-histories-by-support-horizon-and-order](sums-over-histories-by-support-horizon-and-order.md) · [losses-of-the-sum-over-histories](losses-of-the-sum-over-histories.md) · [orders-as-a-sum-over-histories](orders-as-a-sum-over-histories.md).
